{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUhdMr88AAAABUh3YUg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlRslzg-DHiM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlRsl", "number": 112, "title": "Support Issue-based Runs in empty GitHub repositories", "body": "## Problem

GitWeave cannot start an Issue-based Run against a newly created GitHub repository with no commits. ProjectWeave can discover and claim its Issue, but GitWeave fails before any graph Node executes.

Observed with https://github.com/takahirox/sandbox/issues/1:

```text
gitweave: fatal: couldn't find remote ref HEAD
```

The repository had no branches or commits. In `gitweave/runtime.py`, `Runtime.__init__` fetches remote `HEAD` into the Run's input/base ref before executing the graph. An empty repository has no commit for that ref, so even readiness and implementation Nodes never run.

## Expected outcome

Support starting an Issue-based Run from an empty GitHub repository without requiring the user to manually create its initial commit first. Once initialized, the Run should use the ordinary implementation, publication, review, and merge flow.

Suggested approach:

- Confirm that the repository is genuinely empty. A failed HEAD fetch alone is insufficient: authentication, network, repository-not-found, and a broken default-branch reference must not trigger initialization.
- Create a minimal root commit with an empty tree, without inventing a README, license, or other product content.
- Establish that commit on the intended remote default branch, then use the resulting remote commit as the frozen Run base. A local root commit alone does not establish the base branch needed by the normal GitHub PR flow.
- Define and document how initialization is enabled and how its target branch is determined. Do not assume every repository uses `main`. Preserve GitWeave's existing separation between core Git operations and GitHub-specific graph/integration behavior.
- Handle concurrent initialization safely. Never force-push or overwrite an existing branch. If another Run or user creates the branch first, fetch and use the resulting remote base rather than creating competing histories.
- Make initialization recoverable: a failure after the remote branch is created must allow a subsequent invocation to proceed normally without repeating or replacing the initialization.

The current failure occurs before graph execution, so adding a graph Node alone will not resolve it. This likely needs a change to startup/runtime handling, or a supported pre-run initialization mechanism; choose the smallest design that fits the existing architecture.

Validate with automated tests covering a truly empty remote, the subsequent normal Run/branch history, concurrent initialization, interruption and rerun, and network/authentication failures that must not initialize anything. Preserve behavior for repositories that already have commits and for PR-based Runs. Verify that the published work shares the initialized remote base and can follow the normal PR path; do not claim a live GitHub PR test was performed unless it actually was.

## Context

- Source of the failure: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/gitweave/runtime.py (`Runtime.__init__`, remote base fetch).
- Git storage already provides root-commit creation through `Git.commit(tree, parents, message)` with an empty parent list; existing tests in `tests/test_git.py` use an empty-tree root commit.
- GitHub PRs compare different branches: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/create-pull-requests/creating-a-pull-request
- This Issue concerns empty-repository startup. It does not request changes to model/provider settings, usage limits, or unrelated workflow behavior.
